title: Seventeen thoughts on an epic repudiation of Donald Trump
gist: Yglesias celebrates a 2026 midterm repudiation of Trump: Democrats won the Senate, a large House majority and a Texas statewide sweep, which he attributes heavily to the Iran war's gas-price spike but also to Democratic moderation on fossil fuels, immigration and girls' sports. He urges Democrats to keep a bipartisan permitting deal alive and notes business fears that Texas' data center boom could stall.

themes.theme: Midterm outcome and control of Congress

insights.claim: Democrats won a Senate majority in the 2026 midterms, which Yglesias has called the most important thing in American politics for two years.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Divided government with a Democratic Senate constrains Trump's agenda, nominations and legislation through 2028.
insights.quote: Democrats found a way to win a Senate majority
insights.locator: I’ve been saying for two years

insights.claim: Democrats also won a huge House majority, comfortable enough to avoid a dozen hard-left members holding Hakeem Jeffries' speakership hostage.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: A large majority reduces fringe leverage, making House leadership more able to cut deals.
insights.quote: The hard left was semi-openly hoping for a narrow majority
insights.locator: A huge House majority is also nice!

insights.claim: ME-2 was the only House seat to flip from blue to red, after Democrats replaced Jared Golden with Bernie-endorsed Matt Dunlap, who lost despite the blue wave.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Ideological candidate choice in swing seats remains costly even in wave years.
insights.quote: The real ideological fuckup was in ME-2
insights.locator: At the same time, Josh Shapiro

insights.claim: Democrats swept statewide elections in Texas, and Yglesias expects Gina Hinojosa to become a huge star.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: A Democratic Texas statewide executive is a major shift for energy, tech and business-climate policy in a key state.
insights.quote: Democrats sweeping statewide elections in Texas seems huge

insights.claim: Business people are semi-panicked that Hinojosa will halt Texas' data center boom, though Yglesias is unsure how true that is.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Watch Texas data center permitting, grid and tax policy under the new administration — key for AI infrastructure capex.
insights.quote: Business people seem semi-panicked that she’s going to bring Texas’ data center boom to a halt

insights.claim: Yglesias expects Bottoms and Hinojosa to become popular governors because Republican state legislatures will check them, and voters like do-nothing governors.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Gridlocked state governments imply limited radical policy change in Texas and Georgia, tempering business fears.
insights.quote: people just kinda like do-nothing governors

insights.claim: Some predicted a huge Democratic landslide would kill the caucus' appetite for a bipartisan permitting deal; Yglesias argues abandoning it would be wrong after winning on affordability.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Fate of bipartisan permitting reform is a key watch item for energy, transmission and infrastructure investors.
insights.quote: You can’t win a huge landslide on the back of an affordability message and then immediately abandon a bipartisan affordability bill.
insights.locator: A number of people told me

insights.claim: Yglesias attributes much of Democrats' margin to Trump blundering into a war with Iran that spiked gas prices, a factor Democrats cannot count on in 2028.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Energy prices were a decisive political variable; oil price shocks translate directly into electoral outcomes.
insights.quote: How much of Democrats’ margin was provided purely by Donald Trump blundering into a war with Iran that spiked gas prices?

insights.claim: Yglesias pushes back on the view that Democrats only got lucky: candidates' new positions on fossil fuel production, girls' sports and immigration would have been unthinkable in 2022 or 2024.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Democratic moderation on fossil fuel production signals a less hostile stance toward domestic oil and gas.
insights.quote: The things some of the key candidates said about fossil fuel production, girls’ sports teams, and even immigration
insights.locator: I want to push back, though

insights.claim: If the Trump Era ends, Yglesias notes it will be because of moderately high gasoline prices rather than January 6.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Voters punish pocketbook pain far more than institutional norm-breaking.
insights.quote: it will have ended because of moderately high gasoline prices rather than January 6

insights.claim: Candidate quality matters at the margin: Peggy Flanagan's Minnesota performance suggests she would have lost in Iowa or Kansas, though such gaps are modest relative to the national swing.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Candidate effects are second-order to the national environment.

insights.claim: Despite heavy coverage of Haley Stevens endorsing Mike Rogers, Abdul El-Sayed won comfortably, and there are very few single-issue pro-Israel voters, especially after Israel helped embroil the US in an unpopular war.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Israel is no longer an electoral asset; expect weaker pro-Israel positioning among candidates.
insights.quote: there are very few single-issue pro-Israel voters in America

insights.claim: Josh Shapiro's landslide in the Pennsylvania governor race suggests few voters care about Israel from the other side either.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Israel is a low-salience issue in both directions for general-election voters.
insights.locator: At the same time, Josh Shapiro

insights.claim: Dan Osborne's loss in Nebraska was the cycle's most interesting failure: after overperforming in 2024 he lost much of his independent brand and stopped emphasizing conservative immigration views.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Independent brands erode quickly when candidates drift toward party orthodoxy.
insights.quote: The most interesting failure of the cycle is Dan Osborne in Nebraska.

insights.claim: Gimmicks backfired: an Osborne-style independent effort in Montana split the vote, and Alaska's 'find another guy named Dan Sullivan' tactic failed, while winning moderate primaries in Kansas and Iowa worked.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Suggests Democrats will prioritize moderate primary candidates over tactical gimmicks going forward.
insights.quote: Democrats should focus less on gimmicks and more on simply doing the work of trying to have good candidates win primaries

insights.claim: The only impressive Republican performances were Susan Collins (who lost anyway) and the Republican governors of New Hampshire and Vermont.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Breadth of the GOP collapse; even incumbency did not save Collins.
